mainTopic: Teachings about אדם הראשון's creation and sin, and how to answer heretics who claim the פסוקים show more than one God.
overview: This amud is full of אגדה about אדם הראשון and about answering heretics. It begins with where אדם's body was taken from and an hour-by-hour timeline of the day he was created, sinned and was sent out of גן עדן. רב then tells how הקב"ה consulted groups of angels before creating man, and how He keeps bearing with mankind even when people sin. More teachings follow: אדם's huge original size, his speaking Aramaic, and three views of how serious his sin was. This leads to the משנה about knowing how to answer an אפיקורוס. רבי יוחנן limits that duty to a non-Jewish heretic. He also shows that whenever heretics point to a plural word for God, the answer is right beside it. The גמרא then explains the plural 'thrones' in דניאל in three ways. It closes with two stories of answering heretics, one by רב אידית and one by a launderer who learned his answer at רבי מאיר's lectures.

steps.title: אדם הראשון's body came from different lands
steps.stepSummary: The teaching about אדם הראשון's dust continues. His torso came from בבל, his head from ארץ ישראל, and his limbs from the other lands.
steps.simpleTranslation: His torso came from Babylonia, his head from the Land of Israel, and his limbs from the other lands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a teaching that began just before this text. It tells us where each part of אדם הראשון's body was taken from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds detail to the earlier idea that אדם's dust was gathered from the whole world. Here each main part of his body is matched to a specific place. The head, the most important part, comes from ארץ ישראל, the most important land.

phrases.english: His torso was from Babylonia,
phrases.notes: 'His' here is אדם הראשון. The teaching about how his dust was gathered started just before this line.

phrases.english: and his head was from the Land of Israel,
and his limbs were from the other lands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a statement that began before this text, about where אדם הראשון's dust came from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אדם's torso came from בבל, his head from ארץ ישראל, and his limbs from the other lands.

steps.title: רב אחא adds where the buttocks came from
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא adds one more detail: אדם's buttocks were taken from a place called אקרא דאגמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As for his buttocks, רב אחא said: they came from אקרא דאגמא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא adds a small detail to the list from the step before. He names the place where the dust for אדם's buttocks came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier list covered the torso, head and limbs but not this body part. רב אחא fills that gap with a specific local place.

keyTerms.meaning: A place name, in the area of בבל

phrases.english: His buttocks:
Rav Acha said: from Akra De'agma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further body part to the list in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אדם's buttocks were formed from the dust of אקרא דאגמא.

steps.title: The twelve hours of אדם's first day
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בר חנינא goes through the day אדם was created, hour by hour. It runs from gathering his dust until he was sent out of גן עדן. A פסוק supports this: אדם did not stay even one night in his place of honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: The day has twelve hours. In the 1st his dust was gathered. In the 2nd he became a shapeless form. In the 3rd his limbs were stretched out. In the 4th a soul was put into him. In the 5th he stood up. In the 6th he gave names. In the 7th חוה was paired with him. In the 8th two went up to bed and four came down. In the 9th he was commanded not to eat from the tree. In the 10th he sinned. In the 11th he was judged. In the 12th he was sent out. As the פסוק says: "Man does not stay overnight in honor."
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching starts. רבי יוחנן בר חנינא gives a timeline of אדם הראשון's first day, one event per hour, and backs it up with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything, from creation to sin to being sent out, happened within one daytime. The פסוק 'אדם ביקר בל ילין' is read to mean that אדם did not even spend one night in his honored place in גן עדן. The timeline shows how fast he fell from greatness.

keyTerms.meaning: His dust was gathered into a pile
Does not stay overnight in honor

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of this same פסוק is explained in the next step, so the two teachings are linked.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan bar Chanina said:
The day is twelve hours long.
First hour: his dust was gathered,
second: he was made into a shapeless form,
third: his limbs were stretched out,
fourth: a soul was put into him,
fifth: he stood on his feet,
sixth: he gave names,
phrases.notes: He named the animals.

phrases.english: seventh: Eve was paired with him,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמִינִית – עָלוּ לַמִּטָּה שְׁנַיִם וְיָרְדוּ אַרְבָּעָה,
phrases.english: eighth: two went up to bed and four came down,
phrases.notes: אדם and חוה went to bed as two and came down with two children, born right away.

phrases.aramaic: תְּשִׁיעִית – נִצְטַוָּוה שֶׁלֹּא לֶאֱכוֹל מִן הָאִילָן,
phrases.english: ninth: he was commanded not to eat from the tree,
tenth: he sinned,
eleventh: he was judged,
twelfth: he was driven out and went away,
as it says: "Man does not stay overnight in honor."
phrases.notes: תהלים 49:13. Literally 'will not lodge overnight', meaning he did not stay even one night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בַּר חֲנִינָא: שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁעוֹת הָוֵי הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from where אדם's body came from to the timeline of his first day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אדם was created, sinned, judged and sent out all within the twelve hours of one day, as hinted in 'אדם ביקר בל ילין'.

steps.title: A wild animal rules only over someone who seems like an animal
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא explains the end of the same פסוק. A wild animal can only overpower a person who looks to it like an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: A wild animal does not overpower a person unless he seems to it like an animal, as it says: "He is compared to the animals; they are alike."
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא takes the second half of the פסוק from the last step and learns a new lesson from it about people and wild animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'נמשל כבהמות נדמו' are read as 'he seemed like an animal'. Normally a person, created in God's image, is protected from wild animals. Only when he seems like an animal to it can the animal overpower him.

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said:
A wild animal does not overpower a person

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִדְמָה לוֹ כִּבְהֵמָה,
phrases.english: unless he seems to it like an animal,
as it says: "He is compared to the animals; they are alike."
phrases.notes: תהלים 49:13, the second half of the פסוק from the last step.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: אֵין חַיָּה רָעָה שׁוֹלֶטֶת בְּאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the end of the פסוק whose beginning was used in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wild animal has power over a person only if that person seems to it like an animal.

steps.title: God consults the angels before creating man
steps.stepSummary: A memory aid opens a new set of teachings. רב tells that when הקב"ה wanted to create man, He asked a group of angels. They asked what man's deeds would be, and He told them.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory aid: hour, at the end, Aramaic.) רב יהודה said in the name of רב: When God wanted to create man, He created a group of ministering angels. He asked them, "Do you agree that we make man in our image?" They said, "Master of the world, what will his deeds be?" He told them, "His deeds will be such and such."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first gives a short memory aid for the teachings coming up. Then it begins רב's story of הקב"ה asking the angels about creating man. The story is setting up the angels' reaction, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The memory aid lists one key word from each of the next teachings, to help remember their order. In the story, the angels do not answer right away. They first want to know how man will behave, and הקב"ה tells them. Their response follows after this.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid for the teachings that follow

steps.confusionAlert: The words in brackets are not part of רב's story. They are just a memory aid for the next few teachings.

phrases.english: (Hour, at the end, Aramaic: a memory aid.)
phrases.notes: These words are a memory aid. Each one is a key word from one of the teachings coming up.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
At the time when the Holy One, Blessed be He, wanted
to create man,

phrases.aramaic: בָּרָא כַּת אַחַת שֶׁל מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת.
phrases.english: He created one group of ministering angels.
He said to them:
Do you agree that we make man in our image?
They said before Him: Master of the world,
what will his deeds be?
He said to them: his deeds will be such and such.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבְראוֹת אֶת הָאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new series of teachings about the creation of man, introduced by a memory aid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before creating man, הקב"ה consulted a group of angels, who asked what man's deeds would be. The next step continues the story with the angels' reaction.

steps.title: The first two groups of angels object and are burned
steps.stepSummary: The first group of angels quotes a פסוק to say man is not worth creating. הקב״ה burns them, and the same happens to a second group.
steps.simpleTranslation: The angels said before Him: 'Master of the Universe, what is man that You should remember him?' He stretched out His small finger among them and burned them. The same happened with a second group.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues רב's story from step 5. The angels answer הקב״ה's question by saying man is not worth creating, and they are punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5 הקב״ה told the angels what man's deeds would be. Here the first group reacts by quoting a פסוק from תהלים: man is too small and too flawed to deserve God's attention. Their objection is rejected, and a second group that says the same thing suffers the same fate.

keyTerms.meaning: A group (here, a group of angels)

phrases.english: They said before Him: Master of the Universe,
"What is man that You are mindful of him
phrases.notes: תהלים 8:5

phrases.english: and the son of man that You think of him?"
He stretched out His small finger among them and burned them.
And so too a second group.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב's story: the angels' answer after hearing what man's deeds would be.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The angels who said man is not worth creating were burned, first one group and then a second.

steps.title: The third group lets God do as He wishes
steps.stepSummary: The third group learns from what happened to the first two. They say the world belongs to הקב״ה and He should do whatever He wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: The third group said before Him: 'Master of the Universe, the first ones who spoke before You, what did they accomplish? The whole world is Yours. Whatever You want to do in Your world, do.'
steps.whatsHappening: The third group of angels does not object. They say the world is God's and He should do as He wants, so man is created.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The third group does not say man is worthy. They only say that objecting accomplished nothing, and that the decision belongs to the Owner of the world. This sets up the next step, where the angels come back to the question.

keyTerms.meaning: The first ones (the earlier groups of angels)

phrases.english: The third group said before Him:
Master of the Universe,
the first ones who spoke before You, what did they accomplish?
The entire world is Yours.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָה שֶׁאַתָּה רוֹצֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת בְּעוֹלָמְךָ – עֲשֵׂה.
phrases.english: Whatever You want to do in Your world, do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the third group's different response after the first two groups were burned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The third group accepted that the world is God's and that He may do as He wishes.

steps.title: After the flood and the tower, God still bears with mankind
steps.stepSummary: When people became corrupt in the דור המבול and the דור הפלגה, the angels asked whether the first groups had been right. הקב״ה answered with a פסוק saying He will keep carrying mankind.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it came to the people of the generation of the flood and the generation of the dispersion, whose deeds were ruined, the angels said: 'Master of the Universe, didn't the first ones speak well before You?' He said to them: 'Even to old age I am the same, and even to gray hair I will bear,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The story jumps ahead in history. The angels point to how badly people behaved, and הקב״ה answers that He will carry mankind anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The angels' question looks like proof that the first groups were right: man really was not worth creating. הקב״ה does not deny that people sinned. He answers that having made them, He will keep bearing with them even when they fail.

keyTerms.meaning: The generation of the dispersion (מגדל בבל)
I will bear, I will carry

steps.whatToRemember: The angels questioned whether man was worth creating, but הקב״ה created him anyway and keeps bearing with mankind even when people sin.

phrases.english: When it reached the people of the generation of the flood
and the people of the generation of the dispersion,
phrases.notes: These are the people who built מגדל בבל.

phrases.english: whose deeds were ruined,
they said before Him: Master of the Universe,
didn't the first ones speak well before You?
He said to them:
"Even to old age I am the same,
and even to gray hair I will bear, etc."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 46:4

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the angels' objection back later in history and ends רב's story with God's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even when mankind sins, הקב״ה continues to bear with them.

steps.title: רב: אדם stretched from one end of the world to the other
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: אדם הראשון was so big that he stretched across the whole world. After he sinned, הקב״ה placed His hand on him and made him smaller.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said that רב said: אדם הראשון stretched from one end of the world to the other, as it says: 'Since the day God created man on the earth, and from one end of the heavens to the other end of the heavens.' Once he sinned, הקב״ה placed His hand on him and made him smaller, as it says: 'Behind and before You formed me, and You placed Your hand upon me.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching about אדם הראשון begins. רב describes how huge אדם was when he was created and how he was made smaller after his sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads the פסוק in דברים as one phrase: on the day man was created, he reached from one end of the heavens to the other. He reads the פסוק in תהלים to mean that אדם once filled 'behind and before,' and then God's hand pressed him down to a smaller size.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן מִסּוֹף הָעוֹלָם וְעַד סוֹפוֹ הָיָה,
phrases.english: Adam the first man was from one end of the world to its other end,
as it says: "Since the day

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים אָדָם עַל הָאָרֶץ
phrases.english: that God created man on the earth,
and from one end of the heavens to the other end of the heavens."
phrases.notes: דברים 4:32. רב reads the whole פסוק together as describing how big אדם was.

phrases.english: Once he sinned,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, placed
His hand on him and made him smaller,
as it says: "Behind and before You formed me,
and You placed Your hand upon me."
phrases.notes: תהלים 139:5

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן מִסּוֹף הָעוֹלָם וְעַד סוֹפוֹ הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about אדם's size, still on the general theme of the creation of man.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אדם was created stretching from one end of the world to the other and was made smaller after his sin.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: אדם reached from the ground to the sky
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר uses the same פסוקים but says אדם's height reached from the earth up to the רקיע. After his sin he was made smaller.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: אדם הראשון reached from the earth to the sky, as it says: 'Since the day God created man on the earth, and from one end of the heavens to the other.' Once he sinned, הקב״ה placed His hand on him and made him smaller, as it says: 'Behind and before You formed me,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא describes אדם's size using the same two פסוקים, but he measures it differently: up and down instead of side to side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר reads 'on the earth' as where אדם stood and 'the end of the heavens' as how high he reached. So the same פסוק gives a height from the ground to the sky. He agrees with רב that אדם was made smaller after his sin.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן מִן הָאָרֶץ עַד לָרָקִיעַ הָיָה,
phrases.english: Adam the first man was from the earth up to the sky,
as it says: "Since the day

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים אָדָם עַל הָאָרֶץ
phrases.english: that God created man on the earth,
phrases.notes: רבי אלעזר hears 'on the earth' as where אדם's feet stood.

phrases.english: and from one end of the heavens to the other end of the heavens."
Once he sinned,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, placed
His hand on him and made him smaller,
as it says: "Behind and before You formed me, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן מִן הָאָרֶץ עַד לָרָקִיעַ הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second measurement of אדם's size from the same פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אדם was created reaching from the ground to the sky and was made smaller after his sin.

steps.title: Do the two readings contradict each other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the readings of רב and רבי אלעזר clash, since one measures side to side and the other measures ground to sky.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verses contradict each other?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out an apparent clash between steps 9 and 10. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אמוראים use the same פסוק, but one gets a width across the whole world and the other gets a height from the ground to the sky. The question is how the same פסוק can give two different measurements.

phrases.english: The verses contradict each other?
phrases.notes: The two readings of the same פסוק seem to give two different sizes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two readings just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two readings of the פסוק in דברים by רב and רבי אלעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One reading gives a width from end to end of the world, the other a height from earth to sky. The same פסוק seems to describe two different measurements.

steps.title: Both describe the same distance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the distance from one end of the world to the other equals the distance from the earth to the sky, so there is no contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: This and that are one measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by saying both measurements are the same size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two readings do not disagree about how big אדם was. The width of the world and the height from the earth to the sky are equal, so רב and רבי אלעזר are describing the same size in two directions.

keyTerms.meaning: This and that, both of them

steps.whatToRemember: רב and רבי אלעזר agree on אדם's original size and that he was made smaller after his sin. They only describe the size in different directions, and both distances are the same.

phrases.english: This and that are one measure.
phrases.notes: End to end of the world and earth to sky are the same distance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Harmonization: the two measurements are equal
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב and רבי אלעזר give two different sizes for אדם.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both readings describe the same distance, so they agree.

steps.title: אדם הראשון spoke Aramaic
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: אדם הראשון spoke Aramaic, as shown by a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: אדם הראשון spoke Aramaic, as it says: "How weighty are Your thoughts to me, O God."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רב about אדם הראשון: the language he spoke was Aramaic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב assumes this פסוק in תהלים was said by אדם הראשון. The word used for "thoughts" is an Aramaic-style word, so it shows that אדם spoke Aramaic. The next step will back up the idea that אדם is the speaker of this פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Your thoughts (read here as an Aramaic-style word)

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Adam the first man spoke in the Aramaic language,
as it is said:
"How weighty are Your thoughts to me, O God."
phrases.notes: תהלים 139:17. The hint is the word רֵעֶיךָ, which is read here like the Aramaic word for 'thoughts'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן בְּלָשׁוֹן אֲרַמִּי סִפֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new teaching of רב about אדם הראשון, continuing the series that began in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אדם הראשון spoke Aramaic, shown from the פסוק in תהלים that he said.

steps.title: אדם saw רבי עקיבא's generation and said this פסוק
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש teaches that הקב״ה showed אדם every future generation. When he saw רבי עקיבא, he was happy with his Torah but saddened by his death, and he said the same פסוק from תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches what ריש לקיש said: What does "This is the book of the generations of Adam" mean? It teaches that הקב״ה showed אדם each generation and its Torah teachers, each generation and its wise men. When he reached the generation of רבי עקיבא, he was happy with his Torah and saddened by his death. He said: "How weighty are Your thoughts to me, O God."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב by showing from ריש לקיש that אדם הראשון really was the one who said this פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's proof only works if אדם said the פסוק in תהלים. ריש לקיש gives a story where אדם says exactly these words when he sees רבי עקיבא's death. Here the words mean "How heavy this is on me," and they confirm that אדם is the speaker.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what (someone) said, a phrase showing that one teaching matches another
Its expounders, the Torah teachers of that generation

steps.whyThisMatters: It turns a short language teaching into a moving picture: אדם הראשון was shown the whole future and was pained by the death of רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: And this is what Reish Lakish said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"This is the book of the generations of Adam"?
phrases.notes: בראשית 5:1

phrases.english: It teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, showed him
each generation and its Torah expounders,
each generation and its wise men.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.english: When he reached the generation of Rabbi Akiva,
he was happy with his Torah
and was saddened by his death.
He said: "How weighty are Your thoughts to me, O God."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 13 by showing that אדם is the one who said the פסוק in תהלים.
steps.raayaObject: רב's assumption in step 13 that אדם הראשון said the פסוק "וְלִי מַה יָּקְרוּ רֵעֶיךָ אֵל".
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש's explanation of "זֶה סֵפֶר תּוֹלְדֹת אָדָם": אדם was shown רבי עקיבא's generation and said this פסוק.

steps.title: רב: אדם הראשון was a מין
steps.stepSummary: רב says אדם הראשון was a מין, because הקב״ה asked him "Where are you?", which means "Where has your heart turned?"
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: אדם הראשון was a heretic, as it says: "And ה׳ God called to the man and said to him: Where are you?" This means: Where has your heart turned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third teaching of רב: אדם הראשון's sin made him a מין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הקב״ה obviously knew where אדם was standing, so רב reads "Where are you?" as a question about his heart. It means "Where did your heart wander away to?", showing that אדם turned away from true belief. This opens a list of opinions about how serious אדם's sin was.

keyTerms.meaning: A heretic, someone who turns away from true belief

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Adam the first man was a heretic,
as it is said:
"And the Lord God called to the man
and said to him: Where are you?"
phrases.notes: בראשית 3:9

phrases.english: Where has your heart turned?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן מִין הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching of רב about אדם, now about the nature of his sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אדם הראשון was a מין; "אַיֶּכָּה" means "where has your heart turned?"

steps.title: רבי יצחק: אדם hid his מילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says אדם pulled his foreskin forward, covering up his ברית. He proves it by linking the word ברית in הושע to the ברית of מילה in בראשית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: He was one who pulled his foreskin forward. It is written here: "And they, like Adam, transgressed the covenant," and it is written there: "He has broken My covenant."
steps.whatsHappening: A different אמורא gives his own view of what אדם did wrong: he covered up the sign of his ברית מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in הושע says אדם "transgressed the ברית." In בראשית, "He has broken My ברית" is said about someone without מילה. Because the same word ברית shows up in both places, רבי יצחק says אדם's sin was against the ברית of מילה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who pulls his foreskin forward to hide that he is circumcised
It is written here... and it is written there, the formula for comparing two פסוקים

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
He was one who pulled his foreskin forward.
phrases.notes: אדם tried to cover up the sign of his מילה.

phrases.english: It is written here:
"And they, like Adam, transgressed the covenant,"
phrases.notes: הושע 6:7

phrases.english: and it is written there:
"He has broken My covenant."
phrases.notes: בראשית 17:14

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר: מוֹשֵׁךְ בְּעׇרְלָתוֹ הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different opinion from רב's about what אדם's sin was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אדם covered up his מילה, learned by linking "עָבְרוּ בְרִית" to "אֶת בְּרִיתִי הֵפַר".

steps.title: רב נחמן: אדם denied God
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says אדם was a כופר בעיקר. He uses the same two פסוקים as רבי יצחק and adds a third פסוק from ירמיהו, where breaking the ברית means leaving God.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: He denied the core belief in God. It is written here: "They transgressed the covenant," and it is written there: "He has broken My covenant," and they said: "Because they forsook the covenant of ה׳, the God of their fathers."
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא says אדם's sin was the most serious of all: he denied God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן starts with the same link between ברית in הושע and in בראשית. Then he adds a פסוק from ירמיהו where forsaking the ברית of ה׳ means turning to other gods. So for him, breaking the ברית here means rejecting God, not only hiding מילה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who denies the core belief, meaning belief in God

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views of אדם הראשון's sin: רב says he was a מין, רבי יצחק says he hid his מילה, and רב נחמן says he was a כופר בעיקר. The last two both build on the word ברית.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
He was a denier of the core principle.
It is written here: "They transgressed the covenant,"
and it is written there: "He has broken My covenant,"
and they said:

phrases.aramaic: ״עַל אֲשֶׁר עָזְבוּ אֶת בְּרִית ה׳ אֱלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתָם״.
phrases.english: "Because they forsook the covenant of the Lord, the God of their fathers."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 22:9. That פסוק goes on to say they served other gods, which shows breaking the ברית means leaving ה׳.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: כּוֹפֵר בָּעִיקָּר הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third opinion; it uses רבי יצחק's link between the פסוקים and adds a third פסוק to reach a stronger conclusion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אדם was a כופר בעיקר, learned by linking ברית in הושע, בראשית, and ירמיהו.

steps.title: Be ready to answer a heretic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in אבות: רבי אליעזר says to learn תורה diligently and know how to answer an אפיקורוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: רבי אליעזר says: Be diligent in learning תורה, and know what to answer an אפיקורוס.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after talking about אדם הראשון as a מין, the גמרא brings a משנה about answering heretics. This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ties two things together: learning תורה well, and being able to answer heretics. The next step will ask which heretic this means.

keyTerms.meaning: A heretic, someone who mocks or denies the תורה

phrases.english: We learned there (in a משנה):
phrases.notes: This is in אבות 2:14.

phrases.english: רבי אליעזר says:
Be diligent to learn תורה,
and know what to answer the heretic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of אדם הראשון as a מין to how one should deal with heretics.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person must learn תורה diligently and know how to answer an אפיקורוס.

steps.title: Only a non-Jewish heretic should be answered
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the משנה means a non-Jewish heretic. A Jewish heretic should not be answered, because it will only make him more heretical.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: They only taught this about a non-Jewish heretic. But a Jewish heretic, you should not answer, since all the more so he will become even more heretical.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן limits the משנה. Answering is for a non-Jewish heretic, not a Jewish one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jew who becomes a heretic knows what he is rejecting, so arguing with him only pushes him to dig in deeper. A non-Jew may simply be mistaken, so an answer can help.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying a Jewish heretic is less dangerous. It is the opposite: he is more stubborn, so answering him backfires.

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said:
They only taught this about a non-Jewish heretic,
but a Jewish heretic (should not be answered),
phrases.notes: The words 'should not be answered' are not written, but that is what he means.

phrases.english: all the more so, he will become even more heretical.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the משנה just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The duty to answer applies to a non-Jewish heretic. Answering a Jewish heretic only makes him worse.

steps.title: The answer to heretics is always right next to their proof
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that wherever מינים use a plural word about God, a nearby פסוק uses the singular. He gives three examples from בראשית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Every place where the heretics tried to prove their heresy, the answer is right beside it. 'Let us make man in our image', and it says 'And God created man in His image'. 'Come, let us go down and confuse their language', and 'And ה׳ came down to see the city and the tower'. 'For there God was revealed (plural) to him', and 'To the God Who answers (singular) me on the day of my trouble'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a tool for answering heretics: whenever they point to a plural word for God, look close by and you will find a singular word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מינים claim there are many gods because the פסוק uses words like 'us' or 'were revealed'. רבי יוחנן shows that in each case a nearby פסוק describes the same event with a singular word, proving God is One.

keyTerms.meaning: Heretics, here those who believe in more than one god
They acted as heretics, they tried to prove heresy
Their answer is right beside them

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a general rule for reading תנ״ך: a plural word for God is never left alone; the תורה always shows nearby that He is One.

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said:
Every place where the heretics tried to prove their heresy,
the answer to them is right beside it.
'Let us make man in our image' (plural),
phrases.notes: בראשית 1:26

phrases.english: and it says:
'And God created man in His image' (singular).
phrases.notes: בראשית 1:27, the very next פסוק.

phrases.english: 'Come, let us go down and confuse their language there' (plural),
phrases.notes: בראשית 11:7

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיֵּרֶד ה׳ לִרְאֹת אֶת הָעִיר וְאֶת הַמִּגְדָּל״.
phrases.english: but 'And ה׳ came down to see the city and the tower' (singular).
'For there God was revealed to him' (the verb is plural),
phrases.notes: בראשית 35:7. נגלו literally means 'they were revealed'.

phrases.english: but 'To the God Who answers me on the day of my trouble' (singular).
phrases.notes: בראשית 35:3

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁפָּקְרוּ הַמִּינִים, תְּשׁוּבָתָן בְּצִידָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical way to answer the heretics mentioned in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whenever heretics cite a plural word for God, a nearby פסוק uses the singular, which refutes them.

steps.title: More examples: the answer is in the same פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings three more פסוקים where the plural word and the singular answer appear inside the very same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For which great nation has God so near (plural) to it, like ה׳ our God whenever we call to Him (singular)?' 'And who is like Your people, like Israel, one nation in the land, whom God went (plural) to redeem for Himself (singular) as a people?' 'Until thrones (plural) were set up, and the Ancient of Days sat (singular).'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן continues with more examples of his rule. Here the answer is not just nearby, it is inside the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each פסוק, one word is plural (קרובים, הלכו, כרסון) and another word right there is singular (אליו, לו, יתיב). This makes the rule even stronger: the heretic cannot even finish reading the פסוק without seeing God is One.

keyTerms.meaning: The Ancient of Days, a name for God in דניאל

phrases.english: 'For which great nation has
God so near (plural) to it,
phrases.notes: דברים 4:7

phrases.english: like ה׳ our God whenever we call to Him (singular)?'
'And who is like Your people, like Israel, one nation in the land,
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 7:23

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר הָלְכוּ אֱלֹהִים לִפְדּוֹת לוֹ לְעָם״.
phrases.english: whom God went (plural) to redeem for Himself (singular) as a people?'
'Until thrones (plural) were set up,
phrases.notes: דניאל 7:9

phrases.english: and the Ancient of Days sat (singular).'

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי מִי גוֹי גָּדוֹל אֲשֶׁר לוֹ אֱלֹהִים קְרֹבִים אֵלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a stronger set of examples for the rule of רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that the answer to heretics is always right beside their proof.
steps.raayaSupportSource: פסוקים in דברים, שמואל ב, and דניאל where plural and singular appear in one פסוק.

steps.title: Why use plural words at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if God is One, why does the פסוק use these plural words in the first place?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need these (plural words)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a natural question and sets up the answer in the next step. If the plural words only give heretics an opening, why are they written?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We have seen that the answer to heretics is always close by. But the גמרא still wants to know what the plural words mean on their own, since every word in the תורה has a purpose.

phrases.english: Why do I need these (plural words)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the purpose of the plural words just listed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the purpose of the plural words used about God?

steps.title: God consults with His heavenly court
steps.stepSummary: The plural words teach, like רבי יוחנן said, that הקב״ה does nothing without first consulting the heavenly court, as a פסוק in דניאל shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like רבי יוחנן said, for רבי יוחנן said: הקב״ה does not do anything unless He first consults with the heavenly court, as it says: 'The matter is by the decree of the watchers, and the request by the word of the holy ones.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the plural words show that God involves His heavenly court of מלאכים before He acts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural is not because there are many gods. It is because God, Who alone decides, chooses to consult His מלאכים first. The פסוק in דניאל proves that the מלאכים are part of the 'discussion' before a decision.
steps.whatToRemember: Plural words for God never mean many gods. The answer is always right nearby, and most of the plurals show that God consults His heavenly court before acting. The plural 'thrones' gets its own explanation in the next steps.
steps.confusionAlert: Consulting does not mean the מלאכים share God's power. He alone acts; He just involves them first.

phrases.english: It is like רבי יוחנן's teaching,
for רבי יוחנן said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹשֶׂה דָּבָר
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, does not do anything

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִמְלָךְ בְּפָמַלְיָא שֶׁל מַעְלָה,
phrases.english: unless He first consults with the heavenly court,
as it says:
'The matter is by the decree of the watchers,
phrases.notes: דניאל 4:14

phrases.english: and the request by the word of the holy ones.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of why plural words are used.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The plural shows that הקב״ה consults with the heavenly court before acting, as the פסוק in דניאל teaches.

steps.title: Consulting the court does not explain the two thrones
steps.stepSummary: The idea that God consults His court explains the other plural פסוקים, but not 'till thrones were placed.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for all the other verses. But what can we say about 'till thrones were placed'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that one plural פסוק from the list does not fit the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 said the plural words show God consulting His heavenly court. That works for verbs like 'let us make' and 'let us go down.' But 'thrones' in the plural describes objects, not a discussion, so the answer does not cover it.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for these cases)
What is there to say? (asking for an explanation of a case that does not fit)

phrases.english: This works out well for all of them,
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means the other plural פסוקים, which step 23 explained as God consulting His court.

phrases.english: but "till thrones were placed"
phrases.notes: דניאל 7:9

phrases.english: what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that step 23's answer does not cover every plural פסוק
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that all plural words reflect God consulting His court
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Thrones' is a plural noun for objects, not a verb of discussion, so consulting the court does not explain it

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: one throne for God and one for דוד
steps.stepSummary: The two thrones are one for God and one for דוד, as רבי עקיבא teaches in a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: One throne is for Him and one is for דוד, as a ברייתא teaches: 'One for Him and one for דוד,' says רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there are two thrones because the second one belongs to David, and supports this with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural here is not about God being more than One. It refers to two different seats: God's and David's (meaning the משיח). The answer is backed by רבי עקיבא's teaching in a ברייתא.

phrases.english: One for Him and one for David,
phrases.notes: 'David' here means the משיח, who comes from David's family.

phrases.english: as it was taught in a ברייתא:
One for Him and one for David;
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the two thrones
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the plural as two separate seats
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plural 'thrones' cannot be explained by God consulting His court
steps.terutzMaskana: The second throne belongs to David, so the plural says nothing against God being One

steps.title: רבי יוסי: one throne for judgment and one for kindness
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי objects that seating David next to God treats the שכינה as ordinary. Both thrones are God's: one for judgment, one for kindness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said to him: Akiva, how long will you treat the שכינה as ordinary? Rather, one throne is for judgment and one is for kindness.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי rejects רבי עקיבא's reading and offers his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting a human throne beside God's seems to make a person equal to God, which רבי יוסי sees as disrespectful. So he keeps both thrones for God and says they stand for two ways God acts: strict judgment and kindness.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said to him:
Akiva, until when
will you make the Divine Presence ordinary?
Rather, one is for judgment
and one is for righteousness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי עֲקִיבָא עַד מָתַי אַתָּה עוֹשֶׂה שְׁכִינָה חוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי עקיבא's reading and replaces it
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי עקיבא's reading that one throne is for David
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It treats a human as sitting beside God, which takes away from God's honor

steps.title: Did רבי עקיבא accept רבי יוסי's view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי עקיבא took back his view and accepted רבי יוסי's explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did he accept it from him, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a side question about how the argument ended. This sets up the next step, which brings a source to answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We have heard רבי יוסי's objection but not רבי עקיבא's reply. The גמרא wants to know if רבי עקיבא changed his mind.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he accept it from him?

phrases.english: Did he accept it from him
or did he not accept it from him?

steps.triggerLanguage: קַבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ אוֹ לָא קַבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the result of the disagreement in step 26
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי עקיבא changed his reading to רבי יוסי's

steps.title: Another ברייתא shows רבי עקיבא accepted it
steps.stepSummary: A different ברייתא quotes רבי עקיבא himself saying 'one for judgment and one for kindness,' so he accepted רבי יוסי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as it is taught: 'One for judgment and one for kindness,' says רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי עקיבא says רבי יוסי's explanation, which shows he accepted it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the 'judgment and kindness' reading is said in רבי עקיבא's own name. That shows he dropped the David reading and took on רבי יוסי's.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it was taught:
One for judgment and one for righteousness;
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. רבי עקיבא accepted it, since a ברייתא quotes him giving רבי יוסי's reading

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: a throne and a footstool
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה tells רבי עקיבא to stick to complex הלכה. He says the two 'thrones' are a seat and a footstool, both God's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said to him: Akiva, what are you doing with אגדה? Go to נגעים and אהלות! Rather, one is a throne and one is a footstool: a throne to sit on, and a stool for His feet.
steps.whatsHappening: In the same ברייתא, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה rejects the judgment-and-kindness reading too and gives a third explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He sends רבי עקיבא back to the hardest areas of purity law, where he is the expert, and away from אגדה. His reading avoids saying the thrones stand for qualities. They are simply a seat and a footstool, both God's.

keyTerms.meaning: אגדה: the non-legal teachings of the Torah
Two very complicated sections of purity law

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya said to him:
Akiva, what are you doing near aggada?
Go near Nega'im and Oholot!
phrases.notes: These are the hardest areas of purity law, where רבי עקיבא was the great expert.

phrases.english: Rather, one is for a throne and one is for a stool:
a throne to sit upon,
a stool as His footrest.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה עֲקִיבָא מָה לְךָ אֵצֶל הַגָּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading רבי עקיבא accepted and offers a third one
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He feels רבי עקיבא should not be giving these אגדה explanations, and he reads the thrones simply as a seat and a footstool
steps.whatToRemember: Three readings of the two thrones: one for God and one for דוד (רבי עקיבא at first), judgment and kindness (רבי יוסי, later accepted by רבי עקיבא), and a throne and footstool (רבי אלעזר בן עזריה). None of them suggests more than one God.

steps.title: Only someone skilled like רב אידית should answer heretics
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says that whoever knows how to answer heretics as well as רב אידית should answer them, and anyone else should not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Someone who knows how to answer heretics like רב אידית should answer, and if not, he should not answer.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a rule about answering heretics. This sets up the story of how רב אידית answered one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Answering heretics is useful, but a weak answer can do damage. So only someone truly skilled should try. רב אידית is held up as the model, and the story that follows shows why.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Whoever knows how
to answer the heretics like Rav Idit –
should answer; and if not – he should not answer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן הַאי מַאן דְּיָדַע לְאַהְדּוֹרֵי לְמִינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining plural פסוקים to a rule about who should debate heretics
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only someone as skilled as רב אידית should answer heretics

steps.title: The heretic: why 'come up to ה׳' and not 'to Me'?
steps.stepSummary: A heretic tells רב אידית that 'He said to משה, come up to ה׳' sounds like a second power is speaking, since God should have said 'come up to Me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A heretic said to רב אידית: It is written, 'And to משה He said: Come up to ה׳.' It should have said 'Come up to Me'!
steps.whatsHappening: The story begins: a heretic challenges רב אידית with a פסוק that seems to describe two divine beings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If God is the speaker, He should say 'come up to Me.' Saying 'come up to ה׳' sounds like someone else is speaking about God, which the heretic uses to argue for a second power.

phrases.english: A certain heretic said to Rav Idit:

phrases.aramaic: כְּתִיב: ״וְאֶל מֹשֶׁה אָמַר עֲלֵה אֶל ה׳״.
phrases.english: It is written: "And to Moses He said: Come up to the Lord."
phrases.notes: שמות 24:1

phrases.english: It should have said "Come up to Me"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the story that shows רב אידית's skill
steps.kashyaTarget: The belief that there is only One God
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The speaker refers to ה׳ as someone else, which suggests two divine beings

steps.title: רב אידית: the speaker was מטטרון
steps.stepSummary: רב אידית answers that the speaker was the angel מטטרון, whose name is like his Master's, so he said 'come up to ה׳.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is מטטרון, whose name is like the name of his Master, as it is written, 'for My name is in him.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אידית explains that an angel, not God, spoke to משה, so it makes sense that he said 'come up to ה׳.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The angel speaks for God and carries God's name, which is why the פסוק says only 'He said.' Because the speaker is a messenger, he sends משה up to God, a different being from himself.

keyTerms.meaning: The name of a high angel
Like the name of his Master
For My name is in him

phrases.english: He said to him:
This is Metatron,
whose name is like the name of his Master,
as it is written: "For My name is in him."
phrases.notes: שמות 23:21, said about the angel God sends before the Jewish people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the heretic's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the speaker as an angel
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A second divine being is speaking about God
steps.terutzMaskana: The speaker is God's messenger מטטרון, so the One God is not divided

steps.title: The heretic: then let us worship him
steps.stepSummary: The heretic pushes back: if the angel carries God's name, we should worship him too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let us worship him!
steps.whatsHappening: The heretic turns רב אידית's answer against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If מטטרון shares God's name, the heretic says he deserves worship like God. That would again mean more than one power.

phrases.english: If so, let us worship him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אידית's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אידית's answer that מטטרון carries God's name
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Anyone who bears God's name should be worshipped like God

steps.title: 'Do not rebel against him' means 'do not swap Me for him'
steps.stepSummary: רב אידית reads 'אל תמר בו' as 'אל תמירני בו': do not exchange Me for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written, 'Do not rebel against him,' which means 'Do not exchange Me for him.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אידית answers with the same פסוק: it warns not to replace God with the angel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the word תמר as if it came from תמורה, 'exchange.' So the very פסוק that gives the angel God's name also forbids treating him as God.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not exchange Me for him

phrases.english: It is written: "Do not rebel against him" –
do not exchange Me for him.
phrases.notes: A play on words: תמר sounds like תמורה, which means 'exchange.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the demand to worship the angel
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק through a play on words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sharing God's name means sharing God's worship
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק itself forbids exchanging God for the angel

steps.title: The heretic: then why say 'he will not forgive your sins'?
steps.stepSummary: The heretic asks why the פסוק says the angel will not forgive sins, which implies he has the power to forgive.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need 'he will not forgive your sins'?
steps.whatsHappening: The heretic attacks again using the next words of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the angel 'will not forgive' sounds like he could forgive if he chose to. Only God forgives sins, so the heretic says this gives the angel divine power.

keyTerms.meaning: He will not forgive your sins

phrases.english: If so,
why do I need "he will not forgive your sins"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן לֹא יִשָּׂא לְפִשְׁעֲכֶם לְמָה לִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אידית's reading of the same פסוק
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אידית's claim that the angel is not to be treated as God
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק talks about the angel forgiving sins, which only God can do

steps.title: We refused the angel even as a guide
steps.stepSummary: רב אידית answers that we did not accept the angel even as a guide, since משה asked that God Himself go with us.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We hold firmly that we did not accept him even as a guide, as it is written: 'And he said to Him: If Your Presence does not go with us...'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אידית ends the debate: the Jewish people never accepted the angel at all, even just to lead the way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה insisted that only God Himself lead the people. Since they would not take the angel even as a guide, there was never any question of turning to him for forgiveness or worship.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold firmly (literally, 'trust is in our hands')
If Your Presence does not go with us

phrases.english: He said to him: We hold firmly
that even as a guide
we did not accept him,
as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו אִם אֵין פָּנֶיךָ הֹלְכִים וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: "And he said to Him: If Your Presence does not go, etc."
phrases.notes: שמות 33:15. משה asks God not to move the people on unless God Himself goes with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final answer to the heretic
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the angel was rejected entirely
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The angel has the power to forgive and is a power to turn to
steps.terutzMaskana: The Jewish people refused the angel even as a guide and relied only on God
steps.whatToRemember: רב אידית answers each of the heretic's moves from the פסוקים themselves. The angel only carries God's name, must not be swapped for God, and was never accepted at all. Only God led the Jewish people.

steps.title: A heretic questions the wording of the פסוק about סדום
steps.stepSummary: A מין asks רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי why the פסוק says ה׳ rained fire 'from ה׳' rather than 'from Him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain heretic said to רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי: It is written, 'And ה׳ rained upon סדום and upon עמורה brimstone and fire from ה׳.' It should have said 'from Him'!
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. A מין challenges a פסוק that seems to mention ה׳ twice, as if there were two separate powers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only one God is acting, the natural wording would be 'ה׳ rained fire from Him.' Repeating God's name sounds like one power sending fire from a second power. That is the heretic's attack.

keyTerms.meaning: A heretic; here someone who argues there is more than one divine power

phrases.english: A certain heretic said
to Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei:

phrases.aramaic: כְּתִיב ״וַה׳ הִמְטִיר עַל סְדֹם וְעַל עֲמֹרָה
phrases.english: It is written: "And the Lord rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah
brimstone and fire from the Lord"
phrases.notes: בראשית 19:24

phrases.english: It should have said "from Him"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מִינָא לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story with a new מין and a new פסוק, on the same theme as the רב אידית story.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The repeated name, where a pronoun would fit, suggests two separate divine powers.

steps.title: A launderer answers using the example of למך
steps.stepSummary: A launderer steps in and shows that the תורה sometimes repeats a name instead of saying 'my' or 'him,' as when למך said 'wives of למך.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain launderer said: Leave him, I will answer him. It is written, 'And למך said to his wives, עדה and צלה, hear my voice; wives of למך.' It should have said 'my wives'! Rather, this is how the פסוק speaks. Here too, this is how the פסוק speaks.
steps.whatsHappening: An ordinary launderer answers the מין for רבי ישמעאל. He points to another פסוק where a speaker uses his own name instead of saying 'my.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody thinks there were two people called למך. He simply called his wives 'wives of למך' instead of 'my wives.' So repeating a name instead of using a pronoun is just the תורה's style, and 'from ה׳' does not mean a second power.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the way the פסוק speaks

phrases.english: A certain launderer said to him:
Leave him; I will answer him.
As it is written: "And Lemech said to his wives,
Adah and Zillah, hear my voice;
wives of Lemech"
phrases.notes: בראשית 4:23

phrases.english: It should have said "my wives"!
Rather, the verse just speaks this way;
here too, the verse just speaks this way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא כּוֹבֵס שִׁבְקֵיהּ אֲנָא מַהְדַּרְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מין's challenge from step 37.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parallel from another פסוק showing the same style of wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Repeating God's name instead of 'from Him' means a second power.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה often uses a name where a pronoun would fit, as with למך, so there is only one power.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a basic tool for answering such questions: before building a big idea on unusual wording, check whether the תורה speaks that way elsewhere.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל asks where the launderer learned this
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל asks the launderer where he got this answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Where do you have this from?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל is surprised that a launderer knew such a sharp answer, so he asks for its source. This sets up the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not an attack. He simply wants to know where an ordinary worker learned a תורה answer like this.

keyTerms.meaning: To you; here, do you have

phrases.english: He said to him: From where do you have this?
phrases.notes: רבי ישמעאל is now asking the launderer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the launderer's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where the launderer learned the answer from למך

steps.title: The launderer heard it at רבי מאיר's lecture
steps.stepSummary: The launderer says he heard the idea at רבי מאיר's public lecture.
steps.simpleTranslation: I heard it from רבי מאיר's lecture.
steps.whatsHappening: The launderer answers that he heard the idea when רבי מאיר taught in public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains how a simple worker knew the answer. רבי מאיר's lectures reached ordinary people, which leads into the next step about how he taught.

phrases.english: I heard it at the lecture of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He learned it at רבי מאיר's public lecture.

steps.title: How רבי מאיר divided his lectures
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says רבי מאיר's lectures were one-third הלכה, one-third אגדה, and one-third parables.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said: When רבי מאיר would teach his lecture, he would teach one-third הלכה, one-third אגדה, and one-third parables.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the launderer could have heard this at רבי מאיר's lecture by quoting רבי יוחנן's description of his lectures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר did not only teach הלכה. He also taught אגדה and parables, so an idea about how פסוקים speak fits well in his lectures. That makes the launderer's claim believable.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה דָּרֵישׁ רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּפִירְקֵיהּ,
phrases.english: When Rabbi Meir would teach his lecture,
he would teach one-third halakha,
one-third aggada, and one-third parables.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כִּי הֲוָה דָּרֵישׁ רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּפִירְקֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the launderer's claim by describing what רבי מאיר taught.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר's lectures were split evenly among הלכה, אגדה, and parables.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's three hundred fox parables
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds that רבי מאיר had three hundred fox parables, while we have only three.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: רבי מאיר had three hundred fox parables, and we have only three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second statement of רבי יוחנן praising רבי מאיר's parables. This closes the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the last step's mention of parables. רבי מאיר had a huge collection of fox parables, and only a tiny part survived. It shows how much was lost.
steps.whatToRemember: A מין read 'מאת ה׳' as two powers. The launderer answered from רבי מאיר's teaching: the תורה sometimes repeats a name, as with 'wives of למך.' רבי מאיר's lectures mixed הלכה, אגדה, and many parables.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Three hundred fox parables
Rabbi Meir had,
and we have only three.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן שָׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת מִשְׁלוֹת שׁוּעָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second רבי יוחנן statement about רבי מאיר's parables.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר taught three hundred fox parables, and only three are still known.
